newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Senate defeats insurance contribution bill.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Senate defeats insurance contribution bill.

text.p: California's Senate on Thursday defeated a bill that would have barred the insurance industry from contributing to the office of the state insurance commissioner.
The state Senate rejected the bill on a vote of 16-to-22. The bill needed 21 votes to pass the Senate.

The measure, introduced by Senator Quentin Kopp, would have prohibited companies regulated by the state's insurance commissioner, their lobbyists and attorneys from making campaign contributions to the commissioner and candidates seeking that office.
The bill was opposed by the insurance industry.
Kopp's measure was prompted in part by a campaign finance controversy surrounding the current state insurance commissioner, Chuck Quackenbush.
Earlier this year, Quackenbush agreed to pay a $50,000 fine for alleged violations of state campaign contribution disclosure rules during his 1994 campaign.
The state's Department of Insurance did not take a position on the proposed legislation.
